title: Static Purity Rule Analyzer for React Compiler
concept: Rules of React Violation Detection for Compiler Optimization
problemStatement: Implement `analyzeHookPurity(codeString)` that scans a function body for illegal mutations like `props.x =` or direct `state.x =` mutations, returning `{ compilable: boolean, violations: string[] }`.
interviewTrap: If a component mutates existing props or state objects, the React Compiler marks the component as 'un-optimizable' and falls back to standard non-memoized compilation.

testCases.name: Approves clean pure functional component code
testCases.testFn: return analyzeHookPurity('const double = count * 2; return double;').compilable;

details.name: Approves clean pure functional component code

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: The React Compiler analyzes the Control Flow Graph (CFG) at build time, identifying reactive values and automatically wrapping computations and JSX in memo caches, rendering manual useMemo and useCallback obsolete.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Rules of React Violation Detection for Compiler Optimization.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
